contact_edits.before: The one unquestionably triumphant thing about this show is its look. Ken MacDonald's set and Charlotte Dean's costumes transport us to a vanished world where doctors made house calls in evening dress, or indeed to a vanished world where doctors made house calls. Everything that isn't explicitly ghostly is done in shades of grey; the cups in the china cabinet match the upholstery on the sofa. In scale and proportion, this is a paragon among country-house settings, majestic without being overpowering. At the end, when the ghosts turn to poltergeists, the set even gets to do a turn of its own, with furnishings flying all over the place. It could even afford to go on longer and more violently; this is a rare example of Panych erring on the side of restraint. Overall, there's a whiff of superior summer theatre about this winter show, starting with the choice of play. It's Soulpepper punching below its weight. - Blithe Spirit runs until Dec. 15. For tickets and show information, call 416-866-8666.
